title: Methods and parameters (operations and arguments)
hook: A method is a named operation on a type. Parameters are how callers pass data in. Learn ordinary parameters first — value copy for structs, reference copy for classes — before `ref`, `in`, and `out`.

blocks.text: A **method** is a named block of code with a **signature**: its name, parameter types, and return type. The compiler uses the signature to pick the right overload when you call the method. Methods live on classes, structs, and static types. They are how a CSV importer splits rows, an SQS handler processes messages, or a cache service looks up keys.

entries.plainDefinition: A named operation defined on a type. It can take parameters and return a value.
entries.example: `public int Add(int a, int b) => a + b;`

entries.plainDefinition: Two or more methods with the same name but different parameter types. The compiler picks the best match at the call site.
A modifier on the last parameter that lets callers pass a comma-separated list. The compiler wraps it into a collection.
A parameter with a default value. Callers can omit it and the default is used.
entries.example: `char delimiter = ','` — callers can write `Split(row)` without the second argument.

blocks.text: Method design shapes every public API. Overloads let you offer simple and advanced versions. Optional and named arguments keep call sites readable when a method has many parameters. `params` collections (C# 13) accept more than just arrays — but use them for short lists, not as a substitute for a well-named data type.

blocks.title: Return type is not part of overload identity
blocks.body: You cannot overload solely by return type. The compiler distinguishes methods by name plus parameter types (and `ref`/`in`/`out` kind). Two methods `int Parse(string)` and `bool Parse(string)` will not compile.

items.title: Class parameter
items.body: The callee receives a copy of the reference. Both caller and callee point at the same heap object. Mutations through the parameter are visible to the caller.

items.title: Struct parameter
items.body: The callee receives a copy of the data. Mutating the parameter does not change the caller's variable.

items.title: Optional parameters
items.body: Defaults are baked into the caller's compiled code. Changing a default in the method definition does not update already-compiled callers — prefer overloads at public library boundaries.

items.title: Named arguments
items.body: Callers can write `Process(queueUrl: url, maxRetries: 5)` to document intent without reordering parameters.

diagram.title: Parameter passing by type kind
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  C[Caller] -->|class arg| R[Copy reference]
  R --> H[Same heap object]
  C -->|struct arg| V[Copy all fields]
  V --> L[Independent local copy]

blocks.title: Methods in C# vs JS/TS
rows: TS overload signatures are a type-checker fiction over one implementation
`params` is a compiler rewrite into a collection
JS `...args` is a real array at runtime
Baked into caller IL — binary breaking to change
JS defaults are evaluated at call time in the callee
JS/TS use object destructuring or positional only

blocks.title: Ambiguous overloads with null
blocks.body: Passing `null` to an overloaded method can fail to compile because the compiler cannot pick a best match. Cast explicitly or use a named overload.

blocks.title: `params object[]` erases typing
blocks.body: A public API that takes `params object[]` forces callers to lose type safety. Prefer generics or a named collection type when the list has structure.

interviewTakeaways: Overload on parameter types, not return types.
Optional-argument defaults are caller-side constants; changing them does not update old assemblies.
Ordinary parameters copy the reference (class) or the struct data; `ref`/`in`/`out` are the next topic.
commonPitfalls: Ambiguous overloads with null and optional parameters.
`params object[]` that erases useful typing at a public API.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript rest (`...args`) is a real array at runtime. C# `params` is a compiler rewrite into a collection argument. JavaScript has no overload resolution.
TypeScript overloads are a type-checker fiction over one implementation. C# overloads are distinct methods in metadata.
